div.head: ECf 35.1e
div.ab: Unde etiam Occidentales Saxonici, scilicet Execestrenses, habent in prouerbio summi despectus, quod summa ira commotus unus uocat alterum ‘hinderling’, id est ab omni honestate deiectum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 665 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

note.seg: das Suffix ist in æþeling nur -ing nicht (wie in hinderling) -ling; den Irrthum des Verfassers veranlasste vielleicht [ge]lic: similitudo oder likning: Abbild. Da Verf. damaliges hinderling (entartet, niedrig, unecht), das auch bei Orm vorkommt, aus Exeter citirt, so hörte er dort Gebürtige; es lebt noch in Devonshire.

the suffix in æþeling is only -ing, not (as in hinderling) -ling; the author’s error was perhaps caused by [ge]lic: similitudo, or likning: image. Since the author quotes the hinderling of his day (degenerate, base, spurious), which also occurs in Orm, from Exeter, he heard people born there; it still lives in Devonshire.

div.ab: Whence also the West Saxons, namely the men of Exeter, have it as a proverb of the utmost contempt, that one, moved by the utmost anger, calls another hinderling, that is, one cast down from all honour.
